newsitem.title: USA: DeKalb Genetics sees higher FY97 earnings.
newsitem.headline: DeKalb Genetics sees higher FY97 earnings.

text.p: DeKalb Genetics Corp, citing the brisk order pace for its hybrid seed corn, said it expects higher earnings for fiscal 1997 ending August 31.
"We anticipate that in 1997 we will exceed our 20 percent average earnings growth rate objective," said chairman Bruce Bickner in a statement.
To help meet demand over the long term, DeKalb's total capital expenditures could reach $60 million in fiscal 1997, double the level of the prior year, the company said.
The company said it is building a corn drying, shelling and bulk storage facility in Michigan and is making major improvements at its other U.S. seed plants.
DeKalb said capital expenditures are expected to range from $40 million to $50 million in each of the next five years.

"Our seed corn crop exceeded planned production levels, and the commodity price for corn, which is the basis for our grower payments, was lower than expected," Bickner said in remarks prepared for delivery to security analysts at a company meeting.
"Because of the cool, rainy weather that we had experienced throuhgout most of the growing season, this is a far better result than we had anticipated earlier," the executive noted.

DeKalb also said it expects to benefit from an increase in the average corn price of about seven percent, including mix gains. "All told, unit margins in fiscal 1997 are expected to be approximately $4 above last year, which was somewhat depressed from 1995 levels," Bickner said.
In fiscal 1996, DeKalb earned $1.03 per share.
